title: The Town America Left Behind
sources: Wikipedia, 'Centralia, Pennsylvania': coal mine fire burning beneath the borough since 1962; population fell from about 1,000 in 1980 to five in 2020; ZIP code discontinued in 2002; analysts disagree about the exact cause
Pennsylvania DEP chronology: fire began May 1962; trenching, flushing and other control projects had limited results; Congress appropriated $42 million for relocation
David DeKok via Wikipedia / ScienceBlog: most likely started when firefighters burned the town landfill, an old strip-mine pit, in May 1962
Australian Mining Review / Slate (Atlas Obscura): Feb 14, 1981, a sinkhole opened under 12-year-old Todd Domboski; he clung to tree roots and was pulled out by his cousin
ScienceBlog / werelate: more than 1,000 people moved and about 500 structures were demolished
Christian Science Monitor / Discovery UK: enough coal to keep burning for about 250 years

lines.text: Imagine a town where the ground is so hot,
smoke pours out of the cracks in the road.
Well, that town is real.
It's Centralia, Pennsylvania,
and it's been burning underground since 1962.
lines.caps: and it's | been | burning | underground | since | 1962.~nineteen

lines.text: See, it most likely started with a trash fire,
when the town burned garbage in an old mine pit,
and the flames slipped into the coal tunnels below.
They dug, they flooded, they tried everything,
but the fire just kept spreading.
Then in 1981, the ground opened up
lines.caps: Then | in 1981,~nineteen | the ground | opened up

lines.text: under a twelve-year-old boy.
He grabbed a tree root,
and his cousin pulled him out just in time.
So the government paid forty-two million dollars
lines.caps: So the | government | paid | $42 million~forty-two | dollars

lines.text: to move everyone out.
Houses were torn down,
and the town even lost its ZIP code.
Today, only about five people live there,
lines.caps: Today, | only | about | 5~five | people | live there,

lines.text: and the fire could keep burning
for another two hundred and fifty years.
So... would you have stayed?
